summary: @onereach/regular-expressions preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue.js regex-builder component library but declares a preinstall script ("node setup.mjs") that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<ver>/<archive>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, marks the binary executable, and uses execFileSync to run the shipped sibling file math_init.js against it. math_init.js is a ~728 KB obfuscator.io-mangled Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, shuffled string array, hex-named identifiers, rotation function) with no relation to a Vue regex-builder component. setup.mjs itself is likewise obfuscated with hex-named identifiers and per-function string tables that hide the download URL, target filename, and shell commands. Installing the package causes an opaque, obfuscated payload to be executed under a separately-downloaded alternate language runtime on the installer's machine during `npm install`. Using a second runtime to execute a shipped opaque bundle bypasses scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
